items.bodyEn: The Seven-Ri Ferry from Miya landed at Kuwana after 27 kilometers across the bay, roughly four hours when wind and tide allowed. Boats moored beneath Kuwana Castle, and a great torii at the landing marked the entrance to Ise Province, the first gate on the pilgrims' road to the Grand Shrine, which still supplies its timber.
items.sourceNote: 東海道宿村大概帳 (1843): Kuwana-juku, 120 hatago; Hiroshige, 桑名 七里渡口

items.bodyEn: 'I won't fall for that' is その手は食わない, literally 'I won't eat that hand.' Edo wits bent 食わな into 桑名 and tacked on the town's famous dish: その手は桑名の焼き蛤. Grilled hamaguri clams, roasted in the shell at teahouses by the landing, were a Tōkaidō specialty, and the pun still earns a groan today.
items.ja: その{手|て}は{桑名|くわな}の{焼|や}き{蛤|はまぐり}
items.kana: そのてはくわなのやきはまぐり
items.sourceNote: Edo-period 地口 (pun) on その手は食わない; recorded in standard kotowaza dictionaries

items.bodyEn: The つれて in 〜につれて is the て-form of 連れる, 'to take someone along.' The pattern pictures one change leading another by the hand: 年を取るにつれて、物忘れが増える, as the years come, forgetfulness comes with them. Because it describes gradual, parallel movement, both halves must be things that shift by degrees, never a single completed event.
items.sourceNote: Nihon Kokugo Daijiten (Shōgakukan), entry つれて(連れて): 動詞「連れる」の連用形+「て」

items.bodyEn: 〜につれて, 〜に伴って and 〜とともに can all mean 'as X changes, so does Y.' につれて is the most conversational. に伴って suits reports on consequences: 経済成長に伴う問題, problems that come with growth. とともに is the broadest; it also means plainly 'together with' a person, 家族とともに, or 'at the same time as': 春の訪れとともに. Pick by register, then by meaning.
items.ja: {春|はる}の{訪|おとず}れとともに
items.kana: はるのおとずれとともに
